skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Publish text, Markdown, JSON, files, and built static sites to brewpage.app with explicit namespace and password choices.
skill.summary: Create shareable brewpage.app links and save owner tokens in protected local history.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: The static alerts identify documented publishing operations, defensive checks, literal formatting, and protected local history rather than demonstrated attacks. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration, encoded payloads, or audit-directed prompt injection. A separate confirmation weakness can publish changed archive contents without renewed approval.

remediation.issue: Archive approval is not bound to the reviewed content.
remediation.suggestion: Retain a private archive snapshot and bind confirmation to its digest. Reject changed inputs and upload only the approved snapshot.

semantic_findings.title: Archive Confirmation Does Not Bind Reviewed Content
semantic_findings.description: Approval reruns publication with --confirmed, rebuilding directories or rereading supplied ZIPs. Changed sensitive entries then bypass renewed confirmation and can reach the hosting service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The retry flag bypasses every confirmation result without comparing a prior manifest or digest. Exploitation requires source changes before retry or upload.

content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing generated content often requires a separate hosting workflow. This skill publishes selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link after explicit access choices.
actual_capabilities: Publish text and Markdown as rendered pages, valid JSON as documents, and selected files as uploads.
Package built static directories into ZIP archives while preserving relative asset paths.
Inspect site archives with integrity checks, size budgets, entry selection, and filename warnings.
Request namespace, expiration, optional password-file protection, and supported delivery modes.
Store owner tokens and returned publication metadata in permission-restricted, git-ignored project history.
Stage long text in private temporary directories and return the exact server-provided publication URL.
limitations: Requires brewpage.app connectivity and POSIX tools; site uploads also require Node.js and archive utilities.
Publishes built static output, not server applications; it does not build source projects.
Filename screening does not inspect file contents for embedded secrets; confirmation does not bind reviewed archive bytes.
Publications expire and remain subject to service limits; an unlisted namespace alone does not restrict readers.

prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a shareable text page.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: publish a complete static build.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a prepared archive before publication.

Review the manifest and choose whether to publish or cancel.

best_practices: Review built files for embedded secrets and keep inputs unchanged throughout inspection, confirmation, and upload.
Choose visibility and expiration deliberately; use password protection when an unlisted link is insufficient.
Keep owner-token history private and verify the exact returned site URL and asset paths.
anti_patterns: Publishing source projects, credentials, or personal data without reviewing every included file.
Treating an unlisted namespace as authentication or placing passwords directly in prompts.
Approving archive warnings without reviewing them or changing source files after approval.

faq.question: What content can I publish?
faq.answer: Text, Markdown, valid JSON, individual files, built static directories, and prepared site ZIP archives are supported.

faq.question: Does publishing require an account?
faq.answer: The documented publishing workflow requires no account. Account management is optional, and publications still expire.

faq.question: Is an unlisted namespace private?
faq.answer: It is not listed publicly, but anyone with its link can read it without a password. Public namespaces support discovery.

faq.question: How are passwords and owner tokens handled?
faq.answer: Passwords come from selected local files through private header files. Owner tokens are saved in restricted local history, not intentionally printed.

faq.question: Does archive inspection guarantee that content is safe?
faq.answer: No. Inspection checks archive structure and filenames, not embedded secrets. Keep files unchanged after review because confirmation does not bind their contents.

faq.question: Which tools and limits apply?
faq.answer: Use POSIX Bash, curl, jq, Python, and Git where required. Sites need Node.js and archive tools; hosting limits and expiration apply.
